title: Overhaul screen-space reflections
body: # Introduction This PR overhauls the screen space reflection (SSR) implementation for better performance and higher quality: * The main SSR shader has been rewritten to use Hi-Z tracing. This allows rays to cover a much larger range, even with the default 64 max steps parameter. * Roughness filtering is now handled by generating a gaussian-blurred mip chain. This basically removes the need for the roughness quality parameter at no extra cost. * A tone mapper is applied to the reflected color before the gaussian blur to have smoother transitions between pixels with wildly varying luminance. * Instead of separating the specular color and blending SSR with it later, the SSR trace pass now uses the previous frame to obtain the reflected color. The original approach had several problems that this change addresses: * It was executed after everything was already rendered, preventing potential GPU workload overlap with other effects. * Separating the specular color doubled the bandwidth by requiring two render targets. * The specular buffer contained direct specular color, so blending SSR with it removed that information entirely. * The SSR shader did its own fresnel approximation without accounting for the surface's specular parameter, causing visual mismatches between the reflection maps and SSR. * The SSR shader did not use the specular color buffer, which made metallic surfaces appear black in reflections. * The half-resolution SSR buffer is now upsampled to the screen resolution with a surface-aware bilinear filter. * An option for full resolution SSR has been added. # Preview All comparisons were made on a NVIDIA RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU. The fade in/out parameters are also set to 0. ## General Comparison Using Sponza from [here](https://github.com/Calinou/godot-sponza). ### 64 Max Steps |Upstream|This PR (Half)|This PR (Full)| |-|-|-| |268 FPS (3.72 mspf)|323 FPS (3.10 mspf)|233 FPS (4.28 mspf)| |||| ### 512 Max Steps |Upstream|This PR (Half)|This PR (Full)| |-|-|-| |187 FPS (5.33 mspf)|284 FPS (3.52 mspf)|182 FPS (5.48 mspf)| |||| ## Roughness Comparison Using SSR test scene from [here](https://github.com/Calinou/godot-ssr-test). |Upstream|This PR| |-|-| ||| ## Metallic Surface Comparison Using SSR test scene from [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/58616#issuecomment-1054416740). |Upstream|This PR (Half)|This PR (Full)| |-|-|-| |||| # Remarks There'll be visible differences, especially when it comes to roughness filtering and specularity. While the latter is unavoidable (though more accurate), I've done my best to match the former to the original implementation. I didn't have many sample scenes to test with when developing this, so if anyone has complex scenes with glossy materials, it'd be great to see how the PR fares in them. # Questions * The default depth tolerance seems low. In most scenes I tested, 0.2 caused too many artifacts. Since it's also in view space, checking it in the SSR loop currently requires linearizing two depth values. Maybe the parameter could also be defined in hyperbolic Z space? * Decision: Increased to 0.5. * Checking depth tolerance inside the loop allows the rays to pass behind objects, but due to the nature of Hi-Z tracing, gaps from low sample counts can look splotchy. Should users be simply expected to increase the max steps for this, or could we provide a toggle for allowing rays to go behind objects? * Decision: Users should increase max steps, scenarios where this might be noticable are rare. * Now that the roughness filtering is as high quality as it can get, what do we about the option? * Decision: Removed, with the rendering server method deprecated. * Using the previous frame causes the reflections to appear black for a singular frame when the framebuffers get cleared. You can reproduce this by just resizing the viewport. Not sure how this behavior should be accounted for. * Decision: Future work. # Future Work * SSR is currently applied after everything in the forward shader. We can sample SSR first, and skip everything afterwards that contributes to the indirect specular color. I looked into doing this, however indirect diffuse and specular sampling code seemed tightly coupled in a lot of places, so it will likely require careful separation of the logic. * Investigate whether Hi-Z and gaussian-blurred mip chain reductions can be parallelized with shared memory to reduce the dispatch count. At very low mip resolutions, spawning the dispatch takes longer than the actual workload. Similarly, the resolve shader can also write to shared memory to pick samples from neighbors. * The main SSR trace pass shows a large gap at the end where the SM usage suddenly drops. This may be caused by long rays keeping the finished threads in the group idle. Tiling the rays and dispatching an indirect compute workload could potentially solve it. * Investigate how TAA could be utilized when it's enabled. ___ - *Production edit: This closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/66934.*
